newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan minister in secret visit to Europe - papers.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan minister in secret visit to Europe - papers.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign minister John Chang on Monday night flied to Europe for a secret visit, one day after the diplomatically isolated island severed ties with Bahamas, several local newspapers reported on Tuesday.
"Minister (Chang) will be back several days after," the United Daily News quoted vice foreign minister Chen Chien-jen as saying. But Chen declined to reveal any further details.

The China Times said Chang likely will visit Brussels first and then other European countries during a visit that will last more than 10 days. The United Daily News said Chang might also visit unidentified African nations.
Officials were not immediately available for comment.

In a surprise announcement late on Sunday, Taipei said it was ending links with the Bahamas after learning the Caribbean nation was preparing to secure ties with Beijing, Taipei's rival since a Chinese civil war split them in 1949.

After the Bahamas severs ties, Taiwan will have diplomatic links with only 30 states, most of them small, poor and heavily dependent on Taipei's financial largesse. The number soon will fall to 29, as top ally South Africa has said it would switch ties in 1997.
